keyFindings.text: **`app`** — The Obsidian `App` instance (full Obsidian API)
**`component`** — An Obsidian `Component` for lifecycle management (register events, etc.)

**`container`** — `HTMLElement | undefined` — The DOM container the execution can render to. Can be `undefined` (e.g., in code blocks without a render target). If you modify `container` directly, you MUST return `undefined`/nothing to prevent the plugin from overwriting your changes.
**`context`** — `ExecutionContext` — Context object whose shape varies by execution source (see Finding 9)
**`engine.app`** — Reference to the Obsidian `App` (full Obsidian API access)
**`engine.getObsidianModule()`** — Returns the entire obsidian module, enabling `new obsidian.Notice('...')` etc.
**`engine.getPlugin(pluginId)`** — Gets a plugin instance by its manifest id. Returns `undefined` if the plugin is not enabled.
**`engine.importJs()`** imports are cached by the browser; reloading Obsidian may be needed to pick up changes to imported files.
**`engine.importJs(path)`** — Loads an ECMAScript module from a vault-relative path. Returns a Promise. Imports are cached by the browser (Obsidian), so reload may be needed to see changes.
**`engine.instanceId`** — `InstanceId` for this execution (identifies the specific code block instance)
**`engine.internal`** — `InternalAPI` for JS Engine internals (cross-plugin integration)
**`engine.lib.itertools()`** — Returns the [itertools-ts](https://github.com/Smoren/itertools-ts) library for iterator/functional programming utilities.
**`engine.lib.parsinom()`** — Returns the [ParsiNOM](https://github.com/mProjectsCode/parsiNOM) parser combinator library.
**`engine.lib`** — `LibAPI` for accessing packaged libraries (itertools-ts, ParsiNOM)
**`engine.markdown.create(str)`** — Wraps a plain string as a `MarkdownString` so it renders as markdown (not escaped)
**`engine.markdown.createBlockQuote()`** — Block quote element
**`engine.markdown.createBoldText(text)`** — Bold text element
**`engine.markdown.createBuilder()`** — Creates a `MarkdownBuilder` for building structured markdown output
**`engine.markdown.createCallout(title, type, args)`** — Callout element
**`engine.markdown.createCode(text)`** — Inline code element
**`engine.markdown.createCodeBlock(language, content)`** — Fenced code block element
**`engine.markdown.createCollapsibleCallout(title, type, args, collapsed)`** — Collapsible callout
**`engine.markdown.createCursiveText(text)`** — Italic/cursive text element
**`engine.markdown.createHeading(level, content)`** — Heading element (level 1-6)
**`engine.markdown.createHighlightedText(text)`** — Highlighted text element
**`engine.markdown.createList(ordered)`** — List element (ordered=false for unordered, true for ordered)
**`engine.markdown.createOrderedList()`** — Ordered list element (convenience)
**`engine.markdown.createParagraph(content)`** — Paragraph element
**`engine.markdown.createTable(header, body)`** — Table element (header: string[], body: string[][])
**`engine.markdown.createText(text)`** — Plain text element
**`engine.markdown.createUnderlinedText(text)`** — Underlined text element
**`engine.markdown`** — `MarkdownAPI` for creating and rendering markdown content
**`engine.message.createMessage(type, title, content, code)`** — Creates a message in the plugin's message system.
**`engine.message.getMessageById(id)`** — Retrieves a message by its id.
**`engine.message.getMessagesForInstance()`** — Gets all messages for the current instance.
**`engine.message`** — `MessageAPI` for the plugin's message/notification system
**`engine.parseLink(link)`** — Parses a markdown link or wiki link into its components.
**`engine.plugin`** — Reference to the `JsEnginePlugin` instance itself
**`engine.prompt.button(options)`** — Prompts with a modal containing a list of buttons. Returns the value of the clicked button or `undefined`.
**`engine.prompt.confirm(options)`** — Confirm/cancel dialog. Returns `boolean`.
**`engine.prompt.number(options)`** — Number input dialog. Returns `number` or `undefined`.
**`engine.prompt.suggester(options)`** — Fuzzy finder suggester dialog. Returns selected value or `undefined`.
**`engine.prompt.text(options)`** — Text input dialog. Returns `string` or `undefined`.
**`engine.prompt.textarea(options)`** — Multi-line text input dialog. Returns `string` or `undefined`.
**`engine.prompt.yesNo(options)`** — Yes/no dialog. Returns `true`/`false`/`undefined`.
**`engine.prompt`** — `PromptAPI` for user interaction dialogs (text, confirm, suggester, etc.)
**`engine.query.files(query)`** — Runs a callback on every markdown file in the vault, returns array of non-undefined results. Callback receives `(file: TFile)`.

**`engine.query.filesWithMetadata(query)`** — Same as `files()` but also provides `cache`, `tags`, and `frontmatterTags` to the callback. Callback receives `(file: TFile, cache, tags, frontmatterTags)`.
**`engine.query.incomingLinks(file)`** — Returns incoming links to a file.
**`engine.query.outgoingLinks(file)`** — Returns outgoing links from a file.
**`engine.query`** — `QueryAPI` for vault-wide queries (files, metadata, links)
**`engine.reactive(fn, ...initialArgs)`** — Creates a `ReactiveComponent` that re-renders when its dependencies change.
**`engine.resolveLinkToTFile(link, sourcePath)`** — Resolves a link to a `TFile` object, given the source file path for relative link resolution.
**`engine.validators`** — Validators utility object
**`engine`** — The `API` instance (the `engine.*` surface documented above)
**`js-engine-debug`** language variant adds a small debug icon for re-running and viewing stats, without changing execution behavior.
**`obsidian`** — The entire obsidian module. Enables `new obsidian.Notice('Hello')`, `obsidian.Plugin`, etc.
**Errors** in the script are surfaced in the browser console and may render as error messages in the code block output.
**Return `undefined` or nothing** to render nothing (the code block becomes invisible). This is required when directly manipulating the `container` element.
**Return a value** to render it in place of the code block. The returned value can be a string, a `MarkdownString`, a `MarkdownBuilder`, or any markdown element.
